filo update FILE [--dry-run] [-y]

  Reads an exported CSV and applies the file_date, retention and tags you
  changed. retention is a period counted from file_date (7y, 18m, 6w, 30d),
  forever, or a date (YYYY-MM-DD); file_date is a date. keep_until is worked out
  by filo: leave it alone. Dates in the past are fine: the file is then past its
  retention (see filo delete). Rows can be sorted, filtered or deleted, but not
  added. Each tags cell replaces its file's tags, so an untouched cell changes
  nothing and an emptied one removes them all. A row is refused, with one line
  saying why, if a value does not parse, a period has no file_date, the file
  changed since the export, its retention or tags were changed after the export,
  or a tag breaks the spelling rules (see filo help tag). The other rows are
  still applied.

  A changed name cell renames the file in its own directory (never moving it,
  hiding or unhiding it, or replacing another file), if the file is still the
  one the last scan saw; otherwise the row is refused or the rename not made,
  with why (run filo scan and export again).

  If any row clears a retention, removes a tag, names a policy that does not
  exist yet or renames a file, filo lists them first and asks once (-y answers
  yes); no, or no terminal without -y, records nothing at all (exit 1 when there
  was no terminal to ask in).

  A CSV from export retention is read the same way without tags; a blank
  retention there clears a stored one after asking, and without a terminal those
  rows are left alone.

  A tags CSV (from export tags) is told by its header: each tags cell replaces
  its file's tags. Before removing any tag, filo lists those rows and asks (-y
  answers yes); without a terminal, and without -y, it leaves them alone. A row
  is refused, with one line saying why, if for example a tag breaks the spelling
  rules (see filo help tag), the file's tags changed since the export (by tag,
  untag or tags rename), or the file is listed twice.

  A duplicates CSV (from export duplicates) is refused: its decisions are not
  recorded, but carried out by filo delete FILE.

Flags
  --dry-run                check everything and write nothing
  -y                       apply without asking (not for a CSV from export
                           retention)
